text:
Toward the end of last week I placed a number of trades and most completed their run early this morning. Here is one trade taken on eur/usd.

First chart is the 4hr and the blue line is minor support and resistance. Price touched the line at arrow A, hesitated for a short period of time and later pushed strongly through this line, but came back to test it at arrow B. Given the weak looking test I decided to short at arrow C and my target was at 1.24700 and this was hit this morning. This trade is counter to what most of you might consider the actual direction. There are times when I will take the trade if I like what I see.

Next up the 5min chart. The close view of what I saw and my entry marked on the right. Price drifted down and was not being pushed down which suggested no bears interested. I waited for a reaction where the nearest S/R area was waiting, the reaction was spectacular and pinned to perfection the very poor origin of this drift down. This told me two things, the bulls are active and want in turn to see a bearish reaction to this and it was very slow in coming. It took from last Friday to this morning for this trade to finish. It is likely to be the start of a bullish move up into over head resistance and a very important S/R zone. I spoke about this some days ago and closing above that will really push price up if we get to the right area and a close.

I will repeat other comments I made last week, if every man and his dog are short the euro, why are we still looking at stronger bullish moves than bearish moves?

At present I am now long euro/usd and a number of strong indications made me take this trade this morning. On the 4hr and daily you will see plenty fresh air to the left of price and we have a very solid target over head that price must hit. Pro money is at work and will shortly show itself on a 4hr close. What it carefully.

some tales of woe with traders getting wiped out arrived in this thread last week and while this is very unfortunate, it does seem to attract others to pour out their stories. The odd success story you will rarely hear about is actually my eur/usd trade on the charts above. This move was traded by myself a few friends of mine and collectively we had 1000 lots in the market, thats 10,000 euro in actually monetery value. At 10 euro per point times 1000 times the amount of points made (48), you can calculate the earnings yourself. This is not a big move, many others will have made 10's of millions on the same move.

Today I will look for more longs and scale in more than I am already if the signs are there.

It is all in front of you waiting, learn this and have the best job there is.

Success is measured by each successive winning trade and an account building over time. The point was to show it is not necessarily about getting the really big moves, but take what you can from the market when it presents itself. The value of any move is determined by the funds you put in it. That last trade was broken down just to show even small moves make reasonable money if you can spot them every week.

Most day traders will not accept the pull backs on a daily close and have to look within the traded session for entries.

My hint previously was I am looking for euro/usd longs. Why?

We have seen a strong rejection of 5min to 4hr sellers. Only pro money can cause that to happen. Given we do not trade in the same room as these people we need to look for the end of the bears before taking it long. At present the battle is still ongoing and a break higher will not surprise me, and until then I sit on my hands and watch.

author: Doctor
text:
i was recently asked to look over a topic in the school room part of the forum and rather than push the posters thread in a new direction, I decided to put some digital ink here and help you make sense of what order flow is and how it works.

The London close and any other session close is of no significance in the greater scheme of things. What most of you see will typically break down into two common moves, the next session will reverse the previous session, or it will work price to where the next batch of major orders lay. Many times London will close with lots of positioning going on. Some of you will see positioning as the term compression. But it has no defined shape or pattern, it is simply a slow price grind to an entry price area.

Never forget the fundamentals behind price movement, it will only break in the direction where more orders have been placed and the break will leave pending orders behind at the breaking price and these price levels are future targets on all time frames. The higher time frames give the greatest reaction as more of the professional money will be targeting those. Intraday targets are less dramatic in movement unless they happen upon a 4hr+ area of old movement. We know there will always be pending orders remaining to be filled at those now old prices, because the banks and institutions will have been given instructions from their customers to sell currency x and a particular price. The banks and institutions cannot get all the orders into the market at the desired price because it will cause the price to move too far from the desired order price.

Asia tends to have a subdued trading session and only when the EU and London sessions get under way will you get movement, the majority of the worlds money is traded in the London session and a great deal of the good moves happen in that session.

it is better if you dont beat yourself up looking for some secret to any session in particular, because there are no secrets to trading, no special or hidden signals. It is all plain Jane and in your face if you constantly refer to the big picture i.e higher time frame and then drop down for a closer view. I see too many people trying to conduct an of over analysis of what is very simple in reality. There are no banks or institutions that know what way price will break, they know as much as we do and its all right there on the charts. They look for the same things we do and their only edge, and it is a very slight edge, is the bigger players will have custom orders that tell them where their customers want to deal. In the overall picture this information has little validity because it can only be proven accurate after a move. Therefore historical price now becomes an asset to them and all other traders once they know where to look. This is what we do here in case the penny has not yet dropped.

There is also talk going on in this forum about liquidity and there is a very obvious fact which is easily over looked. Books and those who quote from them often state price can only do one of three things, price goes up, price goes down, and price goes sideways. Nonsense!

Price cannot go sideways, price is not a vector and can only rise or fall.

Order flow in the market determines how long it takes for price to move with more vigor than it does when in a period of consolidation. The amount of money traded to make any move happen is not a set amount or even a minimum amount of orders, in the end price will only move where there are more orders placed of a particular type i.e long or short. Nobody knows how many orders of each type there are in the forex market, there is no central exchange and no way to get the order information. Dont waste your time trying to find a way, countless others before you tried ways and all failed.

When price moves, those who were wrong are stopped out, new orders come in from those who are reversing their position and retail traders jump in as price is moving and those who were first stopped out also add momentum to the move with market orders in the direction of the break, mainly retail traders.

All we can do at best is look for historical reasons and apply this to a level or price area for possible future moves. Trading is neither science or art, it is a reflection of what value humans place on a particular financial instrument at a given point in time.

author: Doctor
text:
Supply is normally resistance and demand normally suport. Where it changes is when the level is broken, then you take the opposite view. Broken supply is now new support which is also new demand and the price rises. Some people call this a flip zone or S/R flip etc. The names and terms mean little, the main thing is to train your brain to be aware this can happen.

Take a current pair. eur/usd just broke resistance which means no sellers were willing to take it down and the buyers ran with it. If price makes it back to the break out area it will show support once price action confirms this. The time it takes for support to hold cannot be defined, it can take a single 5min candle or an hourly candle close etc. This ties into your risk appetite.

A clue is often gained on higher time frames where cleaner price action is displayed. Given today is a friday I still hold the view that I said some days back when I was looking for euro longs up to an important resistance/decision area. This area will be watched very closely by pro money for signs of major buying coming into the euro.

If you look on the daily chart this area should immediately stand out to you, if it doesnt. You must engage your logical brain and think like a guy with deep pockets and where do I see the most obvious place to put my money.

Now the current time is 2pm London and I see an hourly candle close with a spike on top. Some people have taken profit on the move and New York open is not far off. We also have a 4hr candle close at 3pm local and then we wait to see what will come about. There is a possibility of selling because we hit an old supply/decision area. Both long or short are options at current time, but I wont short this. I take the longer term view which is still bullish for about another typical days trading, a strong push will not surprise me either with an over head target and only strong bullish candles on the 4hr chart since July 25th.

I mentioned it many times before, this is counter intuitive and the rules change to most peoples eyes which is why I say there are no rules.

author: Doctor
text:
A new trading month is about to begin and here is what to do at the beginning of every month, and each week, day etc.

View and conduct your analysis on...

monthly chart weekly chart daily chart 4hr chart

On each new week

View and conduct your analysis on....

weekly chart daily chart 4hr chart

On each new day

View and conduct your analysis on....

daily chart 4hr chart 1hr chart + lower time frames of interest you with considering your risk and capital funding.

Lets get stuck into what I see on the monthly chart for eur/usd.

The blue purple lines represents support and resistance denoted with an S an R. I know, I spoil you lot rotten. The blue line has more touches and becomes the main line of interest. I will come back to these lines shortly and for the moment cast your eyes on the lower Box B. This is the last place where clean buyers entered the market, I call it clean because we have not had any attempt to come back into that box. Given the time frame being what it is and the support gained later in time and at higher prices, it would take incredibly bad news politically, financially and a war etc to pull price down that far. Given we are in recession the Euro is proving highly immune to lower prices contrary to the media telling us the sky is falling.

Above the blue line I have Box A, my script writer is off for the weekend so excuse the poor dramatic effects in my text. Box A is where few sellers remain, why?....price took most if not all of the sellers with it as it wound lower, therefore any future target we look for on this time frame is much higher and the top of the chart the most obvious place. Can we get there?....possibly, we need Europe to extract the digit and find a way to create virtual money to pay for real debts.

The present state of play on the monthly chart shows a bullish close and pinned support and also gave a nice false break to the down side. Given the world and their granny are short the Euro this move would have made sense to a lot of traders because the move until this monthly close was bearish.

Pay attention to the spike left of current price, see how it pinned the lower purple line? That was perfection to grab the last of the demand (buyers) to its left. Very nice move indeed and would have been seen by pro money as a nice covert long when everyone else was shorting the Euro, you only need to see that red candles close with a long tail which can only mean one thing, major buying was going on and right off support.

Who would have guessed? (c) The Doctor 2012.....there, glad I worked that in this early:)

Now onto the weekly chart, and you do the same at the beginning of ever new week. I dont wish to sound like a broken record but please get this into your heads if you want to get the over all picture. It is far to easy to just look at the daily and lower.

Ok, what have we got here. The lower purple line is a carry over from the monthly and the blue line is also carried over. You can see a better view of price reacting at these lines. Always treat a line more of an area and not a hard fixed line. Price wont always pin the line, but most of the time it gets very close. Markets are far from the chaos most see in a price chart.

I marked off the support and resistance levels and held Box A above to show you where most of the sellers got consumed. If we get up there, pushing through may not be too difficult, just want price action as it reaches the box.

Box C, a new box. Last of the newest seller in the market, but look how far they got and look at the reation, why?....the likely cause is there was already heavy shorting well above those traders and those short sellers shorted into support not far below, not a very bright move on any time frame. What you want it plenty room for price to move and a very obvious target. This will net you more profit in the long term even when trading off low time frame charts. Look for the room for price to move and the target before you pull the trigger.

The last candle is our weekly candle close, what do you see? Well considering I made it easy for you there is no problem is seeing a bullish close and pinning over head resistance. And this tells you what for the new week?....expect a pull back first, but there where?....look down and to the left for an area where you can see the last buyer comes in, or where there is good support. Would the blue line suit you?...or maybe the purple line?...lets look deeper again.

Here is the daily chart.

Box A carried over from the higher time frames and while its a good distance away, always keep it in mind as over head resistance as well as a target if longs look good. The blue line is also carried over and the purple too far down to see it on this time frame. The blue line now shows some order to the chaos, note the support it provided in the past, many hits, therefore it is of significance.

About the blue line is a black line, a lesser line of importance but still price has reacted here with both support and resistance coming in. It was the precursor to the last bullish move last week. Practically pixel perfect. Marked are two D candles, even though more exist, these are the most important that immediately jump out. These are decision candles where price decided it was time to make a move, note how it happens to also be at last Friday's close too, another decision area. Who would have guessed?

Last chart is the 4hr and I have this here just to concentrate your mind as you would on every new week day while trading from here and lower. We get many good signals off this time frame.

The blue line is once again carried over and is seen here to provide strong support. It also have clean and untested demand (buyers) remaining. Above the blue line we have a black line showing resistance at first, then price pushes through strongly and it forms support with a sweet single candle than pinned it nicely. Not going long on that close with such a strong signal would mean trading is not for you, it rarely gets to be much better than that entry.

Above this black line we could draw another horizontal line and you would see price was contained in a range. My upper black line is the top of the price range, but can you see where the lower line would be?.....approx 1.24850 on that chart.

We closed off the week with a bullish candle with no conviction in it at all and this does not surprise me. The end of each day and end of each week will very often show profit taking and this tends to negate the value to us as technical traders in reading that final candle.

A hint prior to the last candle close was a bearish engulfing candle, but there was no follow through and the closed candle sealed the deal for possible shorts. No takers.

We end the week with one candle pinning the upper green line which is resistance and next week I would expect a pull back into support/demand/false break and see can we muster some bulls and new orders with deep pockets would can push price up and through resistance. We will sit/wait and let those guys fight it out and we wont trade until we see at least price at an area of support and price action showing us buying is going on. A counter trend trade may be possible on lower time frames. Exercise caution with going against the tide of pro money.

author: Doctor
text:
Hi Mel,

My entries happen around support/resistance/supply/demand and decision areas. Next time I take one I will grab a few charts and work from the higher time frame down so you can see how it looked. Do be aware that there is little chance of seeing the same physical setup each time, the patterns rarely come up often enough to build a reliable library of setups from, but understanding where the ideal places to trade is where this pays.

I prefer to not use much in the way of buzz words or terms in my trading because it is not needed and only makes it more difficult for others to learn that is going on. I stick to the most basic and universal language used by professional money. Only economists like to use the BS terms, it helps them to sound as if they know what is going on, when in reality there is no way to know until it has happened.

You will not see me use trend lines or moving averages, fibonacci etc. None of these influence price and price will never react to them either. Price is a fixed and hard value and an indicator is a math function based on some guys idea of what the indicator is meant to display. My usual reply about indicators is this.....if I take the 200 period moving average off your chart, has price still moved without it?

Keeping this trading business simple is the key to success. My live charts have zero items drawn on them, totally blank and just candles on it. I use the cross hair to walk around the charts during the trading session to help me find areas as time marches on. The charts I post on here are a reflection of what I saw at the time, but not everything I saw. It would clutter a chart too much if I were to note all the meaning of every candle and area of interest. In time all successful traders develop a mental knack to immediately filter out the noise on a chart and only the important areas jump out at them. I can pick any chart and in seconds see the hot spots. Learning that is done only by spending a LOT of time in front of live charts.

I wandered off your wish a little and I will certainly post a few charts for you during the week. The other info I hope will benefit somebody here.

author: Doctor
text:
fxgangstah, my stop losses for the most part are mental and I do sit and watch my trades as they progress. Once price has moved away from my entry to where I consider it difficult for it to return to my entry price, only then will I place a hard stop. There are other times when price action looks 'settled' and I will place a hard stop. Much of this is in the eye of the trader and there are no hard and fast rules of using x point stops. If your entries are accurate you will often find your hard stops are rather small intraday. I had thought about posting a trade I took on the South Africa Rand last week where I had a hard stop, but I decided not to post up the trade because the wide stop with the Rand's character with major spikes would cause many here to have a heart attack with the draw down and sometimes violent price action.

I never use trailing stops, they are a good way to give points back to the market and cut your trade short. Broker like you to use them, I wonder why?

All my entries happen around support and resistance, supply and demand and decision areas. Anyone who places money in the market away from those area will ultimately fail and become part of the 95+% of ex traders. Once you enter at the correct area you have little draw down and lowest risk. The hardest part of trading is finding the entry, all else is child's play.

My targets are hard set. If the target is a clear old top I will hold the entire trade until it hits that level. If the move looks really nice and a few stroke moments come up, such as a fast spike in the opposite direction, I will look for price action to give me another entry if it coincides with an old area where the same thing happened in the opposite direction, a decision area. Then I will load up more. In the case of monthly and weekly trade signals I will scale in a touch early (low time frame price action) with really small lots and as it starts to move I will load up heavily. My targets for those are intraday and when they close I will again look for more trades in the direction of the bigger picture and only load up on those. The intraday counter trend trades will have lower point targets and hard stops due to the potential of the major players pushing it again. Remember, the pro money does not need price action for the most part, they are the market makers, they make the moves happen and they have the price levels of where they scale in and where the start to close out, and both cannot be done with a single click, they do it slow in the vast majority of trades otherwise the markets move away from them and they loose client money, thats worse than loosing your own in their eyes.

fxfury, the 200ma or ema is often used by the media as a way to guide you. They will say some load of tripe such as price has broken below the 200 ma and the market must be weak. I do not know of a single professional trader who uses any ma as a trade signal. All it means is over time price has come down, but we know that price has come down with supply making it happen and from the highs. You will never hear any person in the media saying price is on yearly highs (say a stock price) and how far can it go down?....we know in forex this is a good place to look for shorts. Stock traders are a different animal and trade often will blind ambition. There are companies out there who are trading on all time highs and their stock prices are still pushing higher. Why would I want to tie up say 300 to 2000 bucks per share on maybe 20 shares for about a year or more and make perhaps 10 to 50k profit, when I can take the same captial and make the same money in a month?

All indicators are FALSE and INCORRECT interpretation of REAL price. Write that on your monitors!

Mel, I am not forgetting about you. During the week I will post some charts up for you.

author: MitchWorse
text:
Most think that price moves towards it's MA, while it's the MA that moves towards price...

When you're one of them, i've got one question: How can an average be leading? That makes no sense!

Lagging indicators(EVERY INDICATOR BASED ON PRICE) won't tell you what price WILL do, they tell what price HAS done, making them obsolete and dangerous. They will cloud your mind with irrelevant data, stealing the focus from what's really going on.

I've learned the hard way, don't waste your time and money.

author: Doctor
text:
True words MitchWorse. It is simply astounding to my eyes to see people accept that a trading system or method states that a moving average has an impact on price, when in fact it is price is the one and only true indicator of value.

Given professional money know the most likely areas where they will filter in and out of their positions, this is where we also look based upon price action in these areas and where others say price is getting support of the x moving average. This is nonsense and bad advice. Price does not get support or hit resistance off any indicator. It only reaches support and resistance off the effect of traders placing and exiting positions at those price areas.

Over many years I have people show me the multi thousand dollar DVD systems/methods and the live courses they attended. Ask one very simple question here........

If the people who sell such courses and materials were as successful as their course material suggests, they would be making far more money trading real money than pushing their wares. Same applies to all the youtube videos people ask me to comment on. All are historical analysis and little substance in the way of future moves and none ever show a partial live trade that is nearing its target. When I post my trades they are live and close to completion. I wont post live entries because it then becomes a signal service and the point of my posts here is to help people get educated and learn to do this for themselves and not depend on me or anyone else.

If a TV channel ever asks me what trading is, I can sum it up in one line.

Trading is price in an area of interest, realised profit is price in an area of interest. (c) The Doctor 2012:)

Learn where the areas are and you got yourself the best business in the world for the price of an internet connection and a computer.

author: Doctor
text:
Most new traders come from their newly found degree in finance. Others come from families with connections with trading firms, big banks etc. Private trading companies will at times run a competition and allow people off the street to apply for a position and the company will take the cream of the crop.

If anyone can understand the how and where to trade and fund an account with sub 10k, within 5 years they should be very well off. Common investment funds believe 16% gain on an account in a year is a good performance. I would consider 16% on a Forex account in a week a poor return. Some weeks will be slow because it takes time for money to get into the market and for the setups to appear. author: Doctor
text:
I cant suggest a risk size, that is a problem only you the trader can answer given your capital and risk appetite. Obviously it is easier to do this with higher funding. From past experience I had taken a new trader's 3k account to average 1k per week profit while he was learning. Risk was.5 lots per trade and all trades taken off the 5min chart. If you look at an established chart where the London session is open for at least and hour and no terrible price action was going on as we saw toward the end of last week, only then can you see clarity and where entries can be pin pointed.

You can also see the average pull back amount and where buyers and sellers came in and left candles with wicks and tails. By all means measure all of these and determine what you feel is an amount of points you consider to be within your funds. I take every trade on the basis that it will fail, and I know before I take the trade how much money I will loose. More importantly, how much money I am prepared to loose. When I win there are no emotions of joy, just get on with the next trade and none of this.....well I would double up cos I done well last time. Money management works for both wins and losses.

I hope this gets you some way towards a risk appetite plan. Taking small bites with a few euro or dollars per trade will build an account in a surprisingly fast period of time. Getting more wins that losses will also grow your confidence and in time you can then go from say placing a 2 to 4 dollar order and work from a 6 to 10 dollar (1 lot) order. The hits when they come wont hurt as bad when you start low. Starting with small amount of real money is always wise and losses are low. In the virtual world you need to make virtual money on a demo account for at least six months before going live. Trade it the same as real money with tiny partial lots and the same risk plan. It does teach valuable lessons without risking a penny. A few will experience losses when going from demo to live, only because their emotions have caught up with them now that the money is real, and theirs.
